tasks.notes: plan-defect: M2 and Proof leg (a) cannot both be satisfied literally. M2 says a non-blank `testCmd` under `--no-baseline` is validated by its runner's probe — "the `TASK_RUNNERS` row whose prefix it matches, else `command -v` of its first word" — and reported as `testCmdRunner` `{cmd, runner, ok}`. Leg (a) uses `testCmd` = `echo NEVER-RAN; false` and asserts `"NEVER-RAN" not in r.stdout`. Since `testCmdRunner.cmd` is the command string verbatim (leg (g) pins exactly those three keys), any line carrying `testCmdRunner` for leg (a)'s command necessarily prints `NEVER-RAN` on stdout, so no implementation inside `skills/ultrapowers/scripts/ultra_run.py` can satisfy both. The implementer resolved this by adding `SHELL_OPERATORS` / `run_wide_runner_verdict` (patch lines 10-33): a command that matches no `TASK_RUNNERS` prefix and contains a shell control operator, redirection or substitution yields no verdict and no `testCmdRunner` key. The divergence is disclosed in `run_wide_runner_verdict`'s and `validate_knobs`'s docstrings and is the sane reading (`command -v cd` for `cd sub && npm test` says nothing about the suite), so it is lawful — but it is a narrowing of M2 that the plan text does not authorize, and the fix lies in the task text, not in this task's FILES. Reconcile by either (i) restating M2 to exempt shell-operator commands the runner table does not know, or (ii) rewriting leg (a) to use a `testCmd` whose non-execution sentinel is not echoed by the JSON line (e.g. a command whose side effect is a file the test asserts is absent, rather than a stdout marker), so M2 can be pinned literally.; The skipped run-wide runner probe is silent. In `run_wide_runner_verdict` (patch lines 30-33) a `testCmd` such as `cd sub && npm test` or `pytest -q > out.log` returns `None`, so `validate_knobs` emits no `testCmdRunner` key and exits 0 — indistinguishable, on the JSON line, from an args file that carries no run-wide `testCmd` at all (leg (j) pins that same shape). For a fail-closed preflight whose Claim is that it "still refuses ... a test runner that is not there", an operator reading the line cannot tell that the run-wide command went unvalidated. Making the skip visible is compatible with every leg and with the additive-keys constraint: nothing pins the absence of a note, leg (a) only forbids `NEVER-RAN` in stdout (a note naming no command text is safe), and leg (j) only forbids `testCmdRunner`. Suggest appending a fixed-text note to `result["output"]` (or a boolean `testCmdRunnerSkipped` key) when `run_wide_runner_verdict` returns `None`, without echoing the command string. Advisory only — the exam is green as it stands.; Disclosed divergence from M2, forced by the plan's own leg (a). M2 says a non-blank `testCmd` under `--no-baseline` is validated by its runner's probe — a `TASK_RUNNERS` prefix row, "else `command -v` of its first word" — with no stated exception. The diff adds `run_wide_runner_verdict` (skills/ultrapowers/scripts/ultra_run.py, new `SHELL_OPERATORS` tuple) which returns `None`, emitting no `testCmdRunner` key and no verdict, whenever the command matches no table prefix and contains any of `; & | newline ` $( ( > <`. Such a run-wide command is therefore silently accepted: `cd sub && npm test` with npm absent passes the preflight green, which is the fail-open case #234's probe exists to close. This is not fixable inside this task's FILES: the plan's leg (a) uses `testCmd` `echo NEVER-RAN; false` and asserts `"NEVER-RAN" not in r.stdout`, while M2's `{cmd, runner, ok}` object echoes the command string verbatim — so no implementation can both emit the key for that command and keep the stdout clean. The implementer chose the only reading that satisfies both, and disclosed it in the `run_wide_runner_verdict` and `validate_knobs` docstrings, so it is lawful; recording it so the operator can settle the text. Fix in the plan: either restate M2 to exempt shell-operator commands the probe cannot read (matching what shipped), or change leg (a)'s `testCmd` to a marker-free command (e.g. `false`) and drop the stdout-marker assertion in favour of `"baseline" not in out`, so M2 can hold without exception.; Advisory, no change required to merge: a run-wide command that shares a runner with a per-task command is probed twice — `run_wide_runner_verdict` calls `probe_task_test_cmds([cmd], probe_wt)` with its own fresh `verdicts` cache, then the per-task block probes the same runner again a few lines later. `probe_task_test_cmds`'s stated contract is "each distinct RUNNER is probed once"; the separate-key requirement in the task Context (`testCmdRunner` is one object, never merged into `perTaskTestCmds`, whose item count existing tests pin exactly) makes the duplicate probe the simplest correct structure, and its cost is one extra `--version` call, so this is noted rather than asked for.; concern: plan-defect: M1 and M2 of the task text are jointly unsatisfiable as written. Since `cmd` is the command string (leg (g) pins it byte-for-byte), any implementation that reports a verdict for that command prints the sentinel. The exam transcribes both legs faithfully, so the contradiction is in the plan, not the exam.; concern: plan-defect: my resolution narrows M2 — a run-wide `testCmd` that matches no `TASK_RUNNERS` prefix and contains a shell operator now carries no `testCmdRunner` key and no verdict, so such a command is not runner-validated (fail-open on that one shape) instead of being validated against a first word that is not its runner. completenessFindings.detail: Task 1, Claim/M2 slot: `skills/ultrapowers/scripts/ultra_run.py:295-313` (`run_wide_runner_verdict`, consumed at line 427-432) narrows the flag's contract below its Claim. M2 states the run-wide `testCmd` is validated by "the `TASK_RUNNERS` row whose prefix it matches, else `command -v` of its first word", and the Claim's sentence is that the check "still refuses ... a test runner that is not there". The implementation adds a carve-out (`SHELL_OPERATORS`, line 292): a command that matches no table prefix and contains any of `; & | newline ` $( ( > <` returns `None`, so no `testCmdRunner` key is emitted, `ok` stays true and the verb exits 0 — that class of run-wide command receives no runner validation at all under `--no-baseline`, where at BASE the baseline run would have caught a missing runner (exit 3). E.g. `no-such-runner-770 tests/ > out.log` passes the preflight green. Graded minor, not blocking: the carve-out is deliberate and documented in the docstring (a `command -v cd` verdict for `cd sub && npm test` would be meaningless), this repo's own run-wide command `python3 -m pytest` matches a table prefix and is probed, the flagless path is unchanged, and the engine's lazy baseline (`fleet/run-engine.mjs`) still surfaces a broken runner at wave time — the defect is that the failure moves later, not that it disappears. No exam leg in `tests/test_ultra_run_task_test_cmds.py` (legs g-l, lines 334-429) covers a shell-operator run-wide command, so the behavior is unpinned as well as unspecified.
